value.name: Asha withholds explanation
value.description: Asha waits silently, deciding that Whitfield's judgment for the one o'clock meeting will depend partly on whether she can endure the moment without explaining herself.
evidence: She waited, because the version of her judgment he carried into the one o'clock would be built partly out of whether she could stand inside this without explaining it.

value.name: Asha remains motionless
value.description: Asha deliberately does not move and fixes her attention on Whitfield's hand and the intake sheet, treating the pause as the whole event.
evidence: Her gaze stayed fixed on the small lift of Whitfield's finger above the intake sheet, on the quarter-inch of air between his hand and the four-eighteen stamp, and she let that distance be the whole of what was happening in the room.

value.name: Asha resolves not to speak
value.description: After stepping back, Asha decides she will not speak again until Whitfield does and holds herself steady in silence.
evidence: She had decided in the half pace back that she would not speak again until he did, and she held to it now with her hands at her sides and her breath evened against the silence.

value.name: Whitfield reviews the records
value.description: Whitfield looks back and forth between the trial record, the intake log, and the page Asha had touched, reading them in the clerk's order rather than Asha's earlier arrangement.
evidence: Whitfield's eyes returned to the trial record, then to the intake log, then to the page he had been touching when she walked in, and the order he read them in was the order the clerk had pressed them, not the order she had given him at nine.

value.name: Silence stretches in the room
value.description: The radiator stays quiet and Whitfield keeps his finger suspended, leaving Asha waiting for him to break the silence with a sentence.
evidence: The radiator stayed quiet, and the finger stayed lifted, and Asha waited for him to be the one who put a sentence into the gap.
